headline: Salesforce has no scope review, but every customer's admin must install your app (a packaged External Client App since Spring '26), and a paid agent must be enrolled in Salesforce's ISV Partner Program and connect through an app you created, not a shared one.

notes: New OAuth clients are External Client Apps. Since Spring '26, creating classic connected apps is off by default and needs a Salesforce Support request; existing connected apps keep working.
An External Client App is local by default: it only works for users of the org that created it until it is packaged and installed in another org.
login.salesforce.com's OpenID discovery lists a registration_endpoint, but an unauthenticated registration request returned 401 invalid_client, so treat registration as manual.
Authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) and refresh tokens is supported. Each customer org has its own instance URL, returned with the token.

paths.label: Your own Salesforce org only
paths.summary: Create a Local External Client App in the org your users already log in to. It works only for that org and needs no Salesforce review.

badges.text: Your org needs an edition with API access: Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance or Developer, or Professional with a paid add-on.

start_here.action: In Setup → App Manager, create an External Client App with Distribution State Local, Composio's callback URL and the scopes you need.
Copy the consumer key and secret from the app's Settings tab and connect a test user from your org.

paths.label: Customers' orgs, installed by each admin (unlisted)
paths.summary: Ship a Packaged External Client App in a managed 2GP package and send each customer's admin the install link. Salesforce does not review an unlisted package, but a paid product must be enrolled in the ISV Partner Program.

gates.title: ISV Partner Program enrolment for commercial use
gates.trigger: You charge for your agent or anything it connects to, or one integration serves several customers' Salesforce orgs. Salesforce's API terms call this Commercial Use.
gates.avoid: Possibly not needed if nothing is charged for, or if you build for a single customer. Read the Commercial Use definition in Salesforce's API terms.

badges.text: Each customer's Salesforce admin must install your package and choose which users may use the app.
Commercial use of Salesforce APIs must go through an app enrolled in the ISV Partner Program.
Salesforce's API terms require a public user agreement and privacy policy for your app.
API-only partners may fall under the Connector Program, which has a fixed annual fee; reports say rates are negotiated case by case.
Each customer org needs API access: Enterprise, Unlimited or Performance, or Professional with a paid add-on.

start_here.action: If you will charge for your agent, apply to the Salesforce Partner Program and ask about the Connector Program. No timeline is published, so start now.
Meanwhile build against a Local External Client App in your own or a free Developer Edition org.
Set up Dev Hub and a namespace, package a Packaged External Client App, promote it and send the install link to a pilot customer's admin.

paths.label: AgentExchange (formerly AppExchange) listing
paths.summary: List publicly on AgentExchange. Adds partner enrolment, business and technology approval, and a security review of about 4–9 weeks, repeated roughly yearly. It is also the route to API access in Professional Edition orgs that lack the API add-on.

gates.title: ISV Partner Program enrolment and distribution agreement
gates.trigger: Required to list on AgentExchange. Your Partner Application Distribution Agreement (PADA) must be signed before you can submit for security review.

gates.title: AgentExchange business and technology approval
gates.trigger: You want a public AgentExchange listing. Salesforce checks your pricing model, listing details and how your package or integration is linked.
gates.avoid: Distribute an unlisted package instead (the customer-orgs path).

gates.title: AgentExchange security review
gates.trigger: Managed packages and Salesforce Platform API solutions must pass Salesforce's security review before they launch on AgentExchange.
gates.avoid: Skip the listing and distribute privately; customers then see a notice that the package isn't authorized for distribution.

wait.note: Trailhead says a solution typically takes 4–5 weeks. The ISVforce Guide gives 1–2 weeks of submission checks, then 3–4 weeks for the first test. A 2023 Salesforce blog cited a 6–9 week queue. Each failed attempt adds a 2–3 week retest.

gates.title: Periodic security re-review
gates.trigger: After approval, AgentExchange solutions are typically reviewed again about once a year, and Product Security can ask for a review at any time.

badges.text: $999 per security review attempt for paid solutions, including each resubmission. Free solutions pay no review fee.
Paid listings use a revenue share (PADA) or, for API-only integrations, the Connector Program's annual fee.
You must join the Partner Community and enrol your solution in the ISV Partner Program.
Salesforce's API terms require a public user agreement and privacy policy for your app.
Even when listed, each customer's admin installs the package and controls who can use it.

start_here.action: Join the Partner Community, enrol your solution and sign the distribution agreement; it must be signed before security review.
Start the AgentExchange listing for business approval while you run Code Analyzer, the Source Scanner and a DAST scan.
Submit the security review (plan for 4–9 weeks; $999 per attempt if paid) and ship the same package unlisted to pilot customers meanwhile.

scopes.what: All data the user can reach; includes every other scope but does not return a refresh token on its own. Composio default. No Salesforce review, but broader than most agents need.
Use REST API and Bulk API 2.0 as the signed-in user. Enough for most agents and the least-privilege choice for customer orgs.
Returns a refresh token so the agent can act while the user is offline. Same as offline_access. Composio default.
Returns an OpenID Connect ID token that identifies the user. Composio default.

prerequisites.item: A Salesforce org where you are an admin with the "Create, Edit, and Delete External Client Apps" permission. A free Developer Edition works; for packaging, a Partner Business Org is safer.
prerequisites.why: The app lives in this org. A Developer Edition Dev Hub that expires takes your packages with it.

prerequisites.item: Every org that connects is on an edition with API access, and each connecting user has the "API Enabled" permission.
prerequisites.why: Professional Edition has no API access without a paid add-on, so many small-business customers can't connect at all.

prerequisites.item: A public user agreement and privacy policy for your agent.
prerequisites.why: Salesforce's API terms require both for any app that uses its APIs.

prerequisites.item: A second Developer Edition org to register your package namespace, plus Salesforce CLI installed.
prerequisites.why: Dev Hub and namespace registration can't be in the same org, and 2GP packages are built with Salesforce DX tools.

steps.title: Checked: Salesforce's OAuth endpoints are live
steps.detail: We fetched login.salesforce.com's OpenID discovery: authorization code and refresh token grants, PKCE (S256), and the full, api, refresh_token and openid scopes are all listed.

steps.title: Join the Partner Community and enrol in the ISV Partner Program
steps.detail: Needed if you charge for your agent or serve several customers' orgs. Apply on the Partner Community; you get a Partner Business Org, which is the recommended home for your app and packages. If your agent only uses APIs, ask about the Connector Program (fixed annual fee). For a listing, sign the Partner Application Distribution Agreement before you submit for security review.

steps.title: Pick the org that will own the app
steps.detail: Own org: use your company's production org. Customer paths: use your Partner Business Org, or a free Developer Edition org. Developer Edition orgs can expire after inactivity, and you then lose the packages tied to them.

link.label: Sign up for a free Developer Edition org

steps.title: Create an External Client App
steps.detail: Setup → Quick Find "App Manager" → New External Client App. Enter the app name (users see it), API name and contact email. Distribution State: Local for your own org; Packaged if customers' orgs will install it. Don't look for "New Connected App": creation is blocked by default since Spring '26.

steps.title: Enable OAuth and add Composio's callback URL
steps.detail: Under API (Enable OAuth Settings), tick Enable OAuth and paste the callback URL below. It must exactly match the redirect URI set in your Composio auth config. If you leave the auth config's redirect field at the toolkit default, register Composio's legacy URL https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add instead.

steps.title: Select OAuth scopes
steps.detail: Under Selected OAuth Scopes add api, refresh_token and openid. Composio's defaults also ask for full; add it only if you keep those defaults. full alone does not return a refresh token, so always include refresh_token.

paste.label: Least privilege (recommended for customer orgs)
paste.value: Manage user data via APIs (api); Perform requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access); Access unique user identifiers (openid)

paste.label: Matching Composio's defaults
paste.value: Full access (full); Perform requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access); Access unique user identifiers (openid)

steps.title: Turn on the web server flow and set token policies
steps.detail: Flow Enablement: tick Enable Authorization Code and Credentials Flow. Security: keep Require secret for Web Server Flow and for Refresh Token Flow; Composio's guide unticks Require PKCE. Click Create. Then Policies tab → Edit → OAuth Policies: set Refresh Token Policy to "Refresh token is valid until revoked", and Permitted Users to "Admin approved users are pre-authorized" if you want to choose who can connect.

steps.title: Copy the consumer key and secret
steps.detail: Settings tab → OAuth Settings → Consumer Key and Secret. Salesforce may ask you to verify your identity. The consumer key is your client ID and the consumer secret is your client secret.

steps.title: Connect a test user from your own org
steps.detail: Connect a user from the org that owns the app. The user needs the API Enabled permission. A Developer Edition org allows 15,000 API calls per 24 hours, shared by every app in the org.

steps.title: Turn on Dev Hub and register a namespace
steps.detail: In the org that owns the app: Setup → Dev Hub → Enable Dev Hub, then Enable Unlocked Packages and Second-Generation Managed Packages (neither can be turned off). In a second Developer Edition org: Setup → Package Manager → Register Namespace. Back in the Dev Hub, open the Namespace Registries app and click Link Namespace.

steps.title: Package the app in a managed 2GP package and promote it
steps.detail: Create a Salesforce DX project, set your namespace in sfdx-project.json, retrieve the app's metadata, create a managed package, build a version and promote it. Keep the OAuth consumer credentials in the owning org; they are not packaged. Unpromoted (beta) versions install only in scratch orgs and sandboxes, which suits a customer sandbox test.

paste.label: Log in to the Dev Hub
Retrieve the app metadata
paste.value: sf project retrieve start --metadata ExternalClientApplication:YOUR_APP_API_NAME --metadata ExtlClntAppOauthSettings --target-org my-dev-hub

paste.label: Create the package
paste.value: sf package create --name "Your Agent" --package-type Managed --path force-app --target-dev-hub my-dev-hub

paste.label: Build a version
paste.value: sf package version create --package "Your Agent" --installation-key-bypass --code-coverage --wait 20 --target-dev-hub my-dev-hub

paste.label: Promote to released
paste.value: sf package version promote --package "Your Agent@0.1.0-1" --target-dev-hub my-dev-hub

steps.title: Have each customer's admin install the package
steps.detail: Send the install URL the CLI prints (https://login.salesforce.com/packaging/installPackage.apexp?p0=04t…). Without an AgentExchange security review, the admin sees a notice that the package isn't authorized for distribution and must confirm. After install, the admin opens the app in External Client App Manager → Policies and chooses permitted users and permission sets.

paste.label: Message to the customer's Salesforce admin
paste.value: Hi! To connect <Your Agent> to Salesforce, please install our package: <install URL>. You'll see a notice that it isn't listed on AgentExchange; that's expected. After install, go to Setup → External Client App Manager → <Your Agent> → Policies, set Permitted Users to "Admin approved users are pre-authorized" and add the permission set or profile for the people who should use it. They also need the API Enabled permission.

steps.title: Run the required security scans and prepare a test org
steps.detail: Run Salesforce Code Analyzer, the Partner Security Portal Source Code Scanner and a DAST scan of your agent's external endpoints. Fix findings or document false positives. Prepare a Developer Edition org with the package installed and your solution documentation for the reviewers.

steps.title: Submit the listing and the security review
steps.detail: Partner Community → Publishing → Partner Console → Technologies: submit your package version for security review, describe your API and OAuth access, and pay $999 if the solution is paid. Create the AgentExchange listing for business approval in parallel.

while_you_wait.text: Build and test against your own org or a free Developer Edition org with a Local External Client App. Developer Edition allows 15,000 API calls per 24 hours.
Pilot with one customer: Salesforce's API terms say an integration built solely for a single customer is not Commercial Use.
Install unpromoted (beta) package versions in a pilot customer's sandbox to rehearse the admin install before you promote a release.
During security review, ship the same promoted package unlisted to pilot customers; they confirm an 'isn't authorized for distribution' notice when installing.

blockers.symptom: Users see OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC, or the redirect contains error=invalid_client&error_description=app+must+be+installed+into+org.
blockers.cause: Since early September 2025 Salesforce blocks connected apps that aren't installed in the user's org, unless the user has Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps or Use Any API Client. This hits Composio's managed app and any connected app you created in your own org.
blockers.fix_now: Ask the customer's admin to open Setup → Connected Apps OAuth Usage, click Install next to the app, then set who may use it. The user then retries.
blockers.fix_properly: Ship a packaged External Client App that each admin installs, with Permitted Users set to "Admin approved users are pre-authorized" and a permission set for your agent's users.

escalate.how: Only the customer's Salesforce admin can install or approve the app. Send them the note below.
escalate.draft: Hi! Salesforce now blocks apps that aren't installed in your org. Please go to Setup → Connected Apps OAuth Usage, find "<App name>", click Install, then edit its policies to choose which profiles or permission sets may use it. Then I'll reconnect.

blockers.symptom: Users from another org see "Cross-org OAuth flows are not supported for this external client app".
blockers.cause: External Client Apps are local by default. A Local app only works in the org that created it; a Packaged app works in a customer org only after that org installs it.
blockers.fix_now: For one pilot customer, have their admin install your promoted package (or deploy the app's metadata to their org with Salesforce CLI).
blockers.fix_properly: Set Distribution State to Packaged, ship it in a managed 2GP package, keep the OAuth consumer credentials in the long-lived org that owns the package, and give every customer the install link.

escalate.how: If the package is installed and the error persists, open a Salesforce case (partners: in the Partner Community) with the package version ID and the app's OAuth settings.
escalate.draft: Our packaged External Client App (package version 04t…, namespace <ns>) is installed in the subscriber org, but the web server OAuth flow fails with "Cross-org OAuth flows are not supported for this external client app". The global OAuth settings live in our org <Org ID>. Which setting links the subscriber's app to our consumer key?

blockers.symptom: There's no New Connected App button, or creating a connected app with the Metadata API fails.
blockers.cause: Spring '26 turned off connected app creation by default in the UI and the Metadata API. Older guides, including Composio's, still describe an "Allow creation of Connected Apps" switch.
blockers.fix_now: Create an External Client App instead (Setup → App Manager → New External Client App). Existing connected apps keep working.
blockers.fix_properly: Plan to move any existing connected app to an External Client App so you don't depend on a feature Salesforce is phasing out.

escalate.how: Only if you truly need a classic connected app: open a Salesforce Support case asking to re-enable connected app creation for your org.
escalate.draft: Please re-enable connected app creation for org <Org ID>. We need a connected app because <reason>. We understand External Client Apps are the recommended replacement.

blockers.symptom: OAuth succeeds, but every API call fails with API_DISABLED_FOR_ORG ("API is not enabled for this Organization or Partner").
blockers.cause: The customer's edition has no API access (for example Professional Edition without the API add-on), or the user lacks the API Enabled permission.
blockers.fix_now: The customer adds the API add-on or moves to Enterprise or higher, and gives connecting users the API Enabled permission.
blockers.fix_properly: If many customers are on Professional Edition, pass the AgentExchange security review; approved apps can then get REST and SOAP API access in Group and Professional Edition orgs.

escalate.how: After your solution passes security review, ask Salesforce through the Partner Community to allowlist your app for REST API in Group and Professional Edition orgs.
escalate.draft: Our AgentExchange solution <name> passed security review on <date>. Please allowlist our app (consumer key <…>) for REST API access in Group and Professional Edition orgs.

blockers.symptom: Older connections for the same Salesforce user start failing with invalid_grant after the user connects again.
blockers.cause: Salesforce keeps only five active refresh tokens per user per app; a sixth connection can revoke the oldest. Password changes, revoking the app, or a refresh token policy other than "valid until revoked" also end tokens.
blockers.fix_now: Reconnect the affected account and delete duplicate connections for the same Salesforce user.
blockers.fix_properly: Keep one connection per Salesforce user per app, and set the app's Refresh Token Policy to "Refresh token is valid until revoked".

escalate.how: Ask the customer's admin to check the app's OAuth policies and session settings for that user.
escalate.draft: Hi! Our Salesforce connection for <user> keeps losing access. Could you check Setup → External Client App Manager (or Connected Apps) → <App name> → Policies and confirm the refresh token policy is "Refresh token is valid until revoked"?

checks.detail: Any admin can create an External Client App in Setup, including in a free Developer Edition org.
Salesforce does not review an unlisted package, but each customer's admin must install it, and a paid product must be enrolled in the ISV Partner Program.
Salesforce has no scope review tiers. Access is limited by the user's own permissions and the admin's app policies.
Only a public AgentExchange listing is reviewed (business, technology and security). Partner Program enrolment applies to any commercial use.
Required for an AgentExchange listing and typically repeated yearly; not required for unlisted distribution.
No install or user cap before approval. Each user can hold five active refresh tokens per app, and API calls count against each org's 24-hour allocation.
Salesforce's API terms require a public user agreement and privacy policy; commercial use requires Partner Program enrolment. No domain verification.
Commercial use requires the ISV Partner Program (revenue share or a Connector Program annual fee); paid listings pay $999 per security review attempt; customers need an edition with API access.
No test mode. Developer Edition orgs get 15,000 API calls per 24 hours and can expire after inactivity; beta package versions install only in scratch orgs and sandboxes.

Security review: 4–5 weeks typical (Trailhead), 1–2 + 3–4 weeks by stage (ISVforce Guide), 6–9 week queue in a 2023 blog; 2–3 weeks per retest. Nothing published for partner enrolment or listing approval.
Salesforce Support (for connected app creation), Partner Community cases, Partner Security Portal office hours, and your Partner Account Manager for urgent reviews.

unknowns.question: What does ISV Partner Program enrolment (or the Connector Program) involve for an API-only AI agent: an approval step, how long, and what fee?
unknowns.why: It decides whether the customer-orgs path is a quick sign-up or a weeks-long commercial negotiation, and what it costs.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Apply via the Partner Community and ask the partner team for Connector Program terms; read the ISV Partner Program Policies.

unknowns.question: Can a paid product connect customers through Composio's shared Salesforce app at all?
unknowns.why: Salesforce's Agent Integration Protocols say commercial use should go through apps created by the developer, which would rule out the shared app for paid agents.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask Composio support how its managed Salesforce app fits Salesforce's terms, and ask your Salesforce partner contact.

unknowns.question: Does a packaged External Client App work cross-org with Composio's callback without extra settings?
unknowns.why: Community reports show "Cross-org OAuth flows are not supported" even after the package is installed.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Install your promoted package in a second Developer Edition org and run one connection through Composio before onboarding customers.

unknowns.question: Exact Spring '26 release-note wording, and whether Salesforce Support still grants connected app creation exceptions.
unknowns.why: The release notes and the related help article render client-side and could not be read; we relied on Salesforce's architect blog and developer docs.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Read the Spring '26 release note on help.salesforce.com in a browser, or ask Salesforce Support.

unknowns.question: Does Professional Edition REST allowlisting apply to External Client Apps as well as connected apps?
unknowns.why: Salesforce's doc describes connected app consumer allowlisting; if ECAs can't be allowlisted, PE customers stay blocked even after review.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask through a Partner Community case once your solution passes security review.

composio_notes.text: Each connection asks for two fields: subdomain (default "login"; if login fails, use the My Domain prefix such as "acme.my", or "<org>.develop.my" for Developer Edition) and suffix.one, which is the API version path (default /services/data/v67.0), not the My Domain. URL_NOT_RESET usually means the subdomain needs to be the org's My Domain.

In Salesforce the path depends on whose org connects, not on scopes. Composio's default scopes (full, refresh_token, openid) trigger no Salesforce review, so composio_default marks the own-org path; for customer orgs, set the auth config's scopes to api,refresh_token,openid and re-test your tools.

Salesforce's Agent Integration Protocols say a developer making commercial use should connect through Connected Apps or External Client Apps the developer created. Plan on your own app before you charge customers.

Composio's own Salesforce guide still offers "Option B: Connected Apps" via an Allow creation of Connected Apps switch. Since Spring '26 that needs Salesforce Support; use Option A (External Client App).
Composio's guide unticks Require PKCE in the External Client App's security settings; leave it ticked only if you confirm Composio sends a PKCE challenge for your auth config.

Composio's docs treat its managed Salesforce app as a connected app. Connected apps used to work in any org, but since September 2025 users without the right permission need their admin to install the app under Connected Apps OAuth Usage first.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.title: Salesforce OpenID Connect discovery (login.salesforce.com)
evidence.excerpt: registration_endpoint: https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/register; code_challenge_methods_supported: S256; grant_types_supported: authorization_code, refresh_token; scopes_supported include full, api, refresh_token, offline_access, openid, mcp_api

probe.summary: Discovery live; registration_endpoint advertised; PKCE S256; authorization_code and refresh_token grants.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.title: Salesforce dynamic client registration endpoint, unauthenticated POST
evidence.excerpt: POST {client_name, redirect_uris} with no initial access token returned HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"invalid client credentials"}
evidence.note: Open self-registration is not available to third-party apps; /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server on login.salesforce.com returned HTTP 404.

probe.summary: Endpoint responds but rejects unauthenticated registration (401 invalid_client).

evidence.label: official
evidence.title: Scope Parameter Values (Mobile SDK Development Guide)
evidence.excerpt: Allows access to the current, logged-in user’s account using APIs, such as REST API and Bulk API 2.0. This scope also includes chatter_api , which allows access to Connect REST API resources.
evidence.note: developer.salesforce.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetchers; excerpt confirmed verbatim with a browser user agent on 2026-10-20.

evidence.title: Scope Parameter Values (Mobile SDK Development Guide)
evidence.excerpt: Allows a refresh token to be returned when the requesting client is eligible to receive one. With a refresh token, the app can interact with the user’s data while the user is offline. This token is synonymous with requesting offline_access .

evidence.title: Salesforce (Composio Knowledge Base)
evidence.excerpt: Use the My Domain or API prefix when login is not enough. For Salesforce, the default subdomain value is login , and that works in most cases. If the default or a simple org label fails, Composio needs the Salesforce login/API domain prefix rather than the full browser URL.
evidence.note: Composio's own documentation; official for Composio toolkit behaviour, not for Salesforce rules. The toolkit's suffix.one field is described in Composio's catalogue as the API version path (default /services/data/v67.0).

evidence.label: reported
evidence.title: Salesforce (Composio Knowledge Base)
evidence.excerpt: Salesforce allows only five active refresh tokens per user per connected app. When the same Salesforce user connects a sixth time, Salesforce can revoke the oldest refresh token, which makes older Composio connected accounts fail with token errors.
evidence.note: Third-party description of a Salesforce limit; Salesforce's own help page on OAuth approvals renders client-side and could not be read.
